convoLines.text: "What's your first memory? Like, ever. The earliest thing."
"Hey — Three. That's young. The brain keeps what it needs, I guess."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Here's the thing: Mine's Columbus, Ohio, I think — heat on pavement, someone's hand huge around mine. Or I invented it. First memories are half real and half the story you needed."
"Still on your first memory."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." "Since Declan died... I keep expecting to see Declan at the fire. Stupid."
"Sleep's gone strange. I sharpen sticks down to nothing at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Do you ever just need to be alone? Like, really alone? Can't sit still, you know?"
"I get it. Solitude's a resource too. Scarcer than food, some days."
"This one — Ground Elder. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"a cellar full of jars — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"I go to the treeline edge and count my breaths. Ten of them. That's my alone. Then I come back — alone is a luxury, and also a little bit a lie. You'd know about that."
"Still on needing to be alone."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Declan is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
You show them Stinging Nettle — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Gotta run. Literally. Bye!"
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"About that question — Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline. It'll pass."
They go still. "So it's not just me. Good. That's... good to know. Bad, but good."
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Lena. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
Counted.
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Lena. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching?"
"Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving."
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Lena. Nobody's settled it."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
There — the story splits again. You mark the spot.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
Counted.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."

"We never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'Sleep's gone strange. I sharpen sticks down to nothing at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning.'"
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Halfway to the cache spot, Arlo freezes. Fresh tracks — big. "We go back now. Quietly." You do. The wild, reminding you.
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Luis. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
Counted.
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Luis. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About the pantry run — I still haven't found anyone. Any chance?"
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. I know the creek bend, past the treeline — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Luis. Nobody's settled it."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
Another crack. The telling doesn't hold together anymore.
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"...Okay. I'll figure it out." They won't ask twice. That much is clear.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
"I've got fires to light — metaphorical ones. Mostly."
"Forget I asked. I'll figure it out."
"Have you — sorry. I keep thinking about them."
They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. "Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything."
"Arlo owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Out there? With YOU leading? ...Let me think about it."
"Sleep's gone strange. I tend the fire without being asked at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
You show them Stinging Nettle — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About the pantry run — still need hands. Are you in?"
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. Nobody's worked the ridge above the creek in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
As I said — Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"Oh — that?" Jovan laughs, relieved. "No, no, you've got it wrong — let me explain..." And they do, and it makes sense, and you feel a little foolish for doubting them.
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Right. I get it." A beat — and then the subject is closed. They won't raise it again.
"Still on that favor."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"Wait, wait —" Jovan holds up a hand, smiling. "I can see exactly why that sounded wrong. No — it's like this..." The pieces slot into place. Of course.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"No — you're right, it's a lot. Forget it."
They nod, already turning away.
"The pantry run — I haven't stopped thinking about it."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. I know where the maypop grows thick — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Landon always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Ella shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"I check the treeline every hour. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Nobody says Landon's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"This cut — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Will you help me clean it?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"This one — Tulsi (Holy Basil). Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"a ridge with a view for miles — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Landon is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Finally. I was wondering when you'd see my value."
You show them Stinging Nettle — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that favor."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

deathBeat: d10: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Declan Park is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d10: 🕯️ Declan Park is dead — dehydration. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
recoverHome: d11: That night, they bring Declan home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d10: ◈ SYSTEM: "Ooh. NEIGHBORS. You know what neighbors are for? STORYLINES. Go knock — worst case, it's CONTENT. Best case? The show gets BIGGER."
d10: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 50. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 4."
d10: SYSTEM: Identification complete. You are 0.3% less lost.
d11: SYSTEM: Codex and inventory overlay online.

d11: ◈ RESONANCE HARMONICS — SYSTEM: "HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED. Objects with high observer-attention waveforms function as auxiliary capacitors. We call this RESONANCE HARMONICS. We do not know why the waveforms taste like grief. We have stopped asking." — Hold a keepsake. Think about them. The System will d
d11: SYSTEM: "DEMONSTRATION. Give me that — Unnamed photograph. WATCH."
d11: SYSTEM: Catalogued. The Codex grows teeth.
d11: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 65. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 5."
d11: SYSTEM: Naming things. Very human. The audience approves.
d11: SYSTEM: Identification complete. You are 0.3% less lost.
d11: SYSTEM: Oh! It has a NAME. You all love names.
burialWindowSay: d10: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+5 integration)
d10: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+4 integration)

d13: You say a few words for Declan. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d13: You bury Declan. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
echoSample: d13: "Good question." "Since Declan died... I keep expecting to see Declan at the fire. Stupid."
d13: "Declan is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
echoV2Sample: d13: The village raises a marker by the fire — Declan, day 13. dehydration. A place to stand.

lastSay: d55: Jovan watches you give the order. "Interesting. Nobody asked me."
d55: Jovan waits until the fire's lit and people are watching. Then, loud enough for all of them: "Who put YOU in charge?"
d55: 📋 Rahim — 🍲 Cook. (a natural — good pick) They'll report back by next part.
d55: "Why are YOU giving orders?" Jovan doesn't raise their voice. That's worse.
d55: Dawn's an hour off — too late for real sleep. Rest a while instead, or wait for morning.
